summary.text: A 60-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and a concealed history of avian exposure was admitted on March 20, 2025 with progressive chest tightness, dyspnea and fever. Examination showed tachycardia, tachypnea, severe hypoxemia, moist rales in both lungs, elevated blood pressure and fever, and she was intubated at bedside and transferred to the intensive care unit.

Laboratory testing showed systemic inflammation, abnormal liver and muscle enzymes, electrolyte disturbance and a markedly elevated d-dimer, with a left calf muscular vein thrombosis, old head CT lesions and left lung solid lesions with effusion. Bronchoalveolar lavage mNGS confirmed Chlamydia psittaci infection, and rooster exposure was identified; the diagnosis became severe psittacosis pneumonia with several complications.

Empirical antibiotics were escalated to omadacycline and moxifloxacin with prone positioning, glutathione, low-molecular-weight heparin and supportive care. On hospital day 10 she developed right limb weakness with an NIHSS score of 8, and MRI showed multiple small new infarcts; heparin was stopped and dual antiplatelet therapy, butylphthalide, edaravone, dexamethasone and rehabilitation were started.

Workup found severe right middle cerebral artery M1 stenosis unrelated to the infarcted area, sinus rhythm and no abnormalities in the immunologic and lipid tests listed. Muscle strength improved to grade 3 in the right upper limb and grade 4 in the right lower limb by April 8, predischarge laboratory values improved, and she was discharged for further rehabilitation training.
